liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cassidy** (1 review): The Cassidy performance is highlighted as a standout moment [16]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): One of the best Music Never Stopped performances the listener has ever heard [21]
- **Help On The Way** (1 review): One of the best Help to Slipknot jams of 1977 [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-06-09.28614.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 167 min; rated 4.79/5 by 86 [1]
- **gd1977-06-09.sbd.fishman.3869.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 175 min; rated 5/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1977-06-09.mtx.seamons.98801.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 169 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [4]
- **gd77-06-09.sbd.murphy.5597.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 163 min; rated 4.85/5 by 27 [5]. Said about its sound: The recording has awesome quality and a challenging, excellent segue between songs; The Sunrise patch comes from a degraded SBD source [20][21]
- **gd1977-06-09.sbd.john-dauria.1409.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 165 min [6]. Said about its sound: Slight dropouts occur in Saint Stephen, Sugar Magnolia, and One More Saturday Night [6]
- **gd77-06-09.akg-bertrando.winters.26450.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 158 min; rated 4.84/5 by 25 [10]. Said about its sound: The audience recording is full of psychedelic fun and the hiss is acceptable [22]

## Around the show

- Steve Marcus of the Dead's staff considers this his all-time favorite show [12]
- An audience member on acid shouted requests throughout the first set until Funiculi Funicula [15]
- The St. Stephen to Not Fade Away sequence rivals the Cornell May 8, 1977 performance [11]
- Second set combines the best songs normally played in 1977 second sets [14]
- The Help to Slipknot to Franklin's jam outperforms the October 11, 1977 version [16]
- The October 11, 1977 Help to Slipknot to Franklin's jam is superior to this one [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-06-09.28614.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Transferred and edited by Charlie Miller from a 7-inch master reel to FLAC [1]
- **gd1977-06-09.sbd.fishman.3869.sbeok.shnf**: source: Reel SBD>Reel>PCM>DAT>DAT>CD [2]. Also: Transferred from a first-generation reel to PCM, then DAT, and finally to CD [2]
- **gd1977-06-09.mtx.seamons.98801.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [4]. Also: Recorded by Dr. Rob Bertrando using AKG D220s and a Tandberg 10XD [4]
- **gd77-06-09.sbd.murphy.5597.sbefail.shnf**: source: SBD hybrid source, including encore: retracking of previous shn set with encore patched in from another previous shn set [5]. Also: A copy of the cassette was donated from the vault by Steven Marcus [18]
- **gd1977-06-09.sbd.john-dauria.1409.shnf**: transferred by John D'Auria; source: Master Reels>PCM>DAT>Delta DiO 2496>Sound Forge 4.5>CDWAV>SH [6]
- **gd77-06-09.akg-bertrando.winters.26450.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Rob Bertrando; source: Audience Recording: AKG D220s [10]

## Art and photos

- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 6/9/77 Winterland Arena, San F…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27364901035/) [24]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27364901035/) [25]
